transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

On a vented dryer, restricted airflow can overheat it and operate the thermal cut-out, giving exactly a turning drum with cold air. 1. Check the programme: make sure it is not set to Cool Air, Refresh, Delicates or a low-heat option. Try a normal cotton/high-heat programme. 2. With the dryer switched off and unplugged, remove and clean the fluff filter. Check the vent hose behind the dryer is not crushed, kinked or packed with lint, and that the outside vent flap is able to open. This matters because poor airflow can cause an overheat cut-out. 3. Run it again on normal heat for 10–15 minutes. If it is still genuinely blowing cold while the drum turns, the heater element or its thermal protection is the leading cause; a failed blower/fan is less likely if there is a strong airflow at the outlet. If the filter and hose are clear and it remains cold, it needs an isolated continuity test of the heater and thermal cut-out, or an engineer. Replace the failed component only once that test identifies it; the element and thermal cut-out are the usual parts to inspect together.

Cleaned the filter and the hose (it was full of fluff, sagging bit especially). Airflow at the hose end is decent now but it's still cold after 20 min. I haven't got a multimeter, so what part should I order?

The blocked, sagging vent makes the thermal cut-out/thermostat the leading suspect, but an open-circuit heater element gives exactly the same symptom. Both need an isolated continuity test to tell them apart. Because you do not have a meter, the sensible next step is an engineer to test the heater element and thermal protection together. If the cut-out has failed, the engineer should also check the thermostat and that the vent run is now short, supported and clear; otherwise the replacement can overheat again. The airflow now being decent makes a failed blower less likely. Avoid fitting a heater element or cut-out based only on the symptoms, as you could buy the wrong component and the exact item depends on the full model number from the rating label.

candidates: Heater element or its thermal cut-out/thermostat failure (high)
Restricted airflow from a blocked filter or vent hose (medium)
